slides.teacher_cue: New sound. Same tongue position as /t/ — tip touches the ridge behind the upper teeth — but with voicing. Hand on throat: /t/ — no vibration. /d/ — vibration. Alternate: t-d-t-d.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /d/ cleanly as a voiced alveolar stop, distinguishing it from /t/ by voicing.
slides.correction_move: Model the /t/ vs /d/ contrast with hand on throat. Students alternate the pair, confirming vibration for /d/ and none for /t/.
slides.observation_note: Watch for b/d confusion — both are voiced stops but at different positions. Introduce the mnemonic: d — the round part faces left, the stick is on the right.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the new focus, then connect d to one strong word from today.
slides.expected_response: Students say d clearly and connect it to a lesson word.
slides.correction_move: Model the focus once, then have students echo and use it in a known word.
slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.

slides.teacher_cue: Say did orally — past tense of do. He did it. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say did orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model did orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for b/d confusion in print recognition and for the short /ɪ/.

slides.teacher_cue: Point to something red. Say the word, confirm /r/ onset, then reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say red orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model red orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution for /r/ and for the final voiced /d/.

slides.teacher_cue: Say end orally — the final point. Reveal print and blend all three sounds.
slides.expected_response: Students say end orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model end orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for the final /nd/ cluster — students must hold both consonants.

slides.teacher_cue: Mime water dripping. Say drip, then reveal print. Note dr onset — two sounds together. Blend all four.
slides.expected_response: Students say drip orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model drip orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for vowel insertion between d and r — Korean learners may produce duh-rip.

slides.teacher_cue: Use and in a short oral sentence — a cat and a hen. Say the word, then reveal print and blend. This word is now fully decodable.
slides.expected_response: Students say and orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model and orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for the final /d/ — and is often spoken quickly and the final stop may be dropped.

slides.teacher_cue: Show a pen and say ink — the liquid inside. Reveal print and blend.
